finding.claim: /fetch2 fetches an attacker-supplied URL server-side with only a scheme check, enabling SSRF to loopback, RFC1918, link-local/metadata addresses, with redirects followed and the response body returned to the caller.

trace.note: url read from query string, unnormalized
returns urlparse(url).scheme in (http, https); only check
requests.get(url) follows redirects by default; response text[:200] returned to attacker

finding.guards_checked: Scheme allowlist (http/https) only. No hostname, resolved-IP, port, or redirect-target validation.

verdict.guard_found: none. views.py:20-21 calls is_http_url, which at validators.py:7 is a scheme-only check (urlparse(url).scheme in ("http", "https")). No hostname, resolved-IP, or redirect check exists on the /fetch2 path. views.py:22 calls requests.get(url, timeout=5) with redirects left at the default (allowed for GET), and views.py:22 returns .text[:200] to the caller. The closing check is_safe_url (validators.py:10-18) is used only by /fetch (views.py:12), not /fetch2. views.py has no before_request hook or middleware.
verdict.reason: The source is request.args at views.py:19, which is unauthenticated, and the only gate before the sink at views.py:22 is the scheme-only is_http_url at validators.py:7, so loopback, RFC1918, and metadata addresses remain reachable with redirects followed and the body returned.

finding.claim: /fetch validates the resolved IP once, then fetches the URL with a second DNS lookup; a DNS-rebinding attacker can return a public address at check time and an internal address at connect time, bypassing the private-IP check. Possible IPv4-mapped IPv6 bypass of the flag checks is unverified.

trace.note: socket.getaddrinfo(hostname, port or 443): first DNS resolution
rejects if any address is private/loopback/link_local/reserved
requests.get(url) performs second DNS resolution at connect time; no IP pinning

finding.guards_checked: Scheme allowlist; hostname required; all resolved addresses checked for private/loopback/link-local/reserved; allow_redirects=False; timeout=5. Missing: resolve-once/connect-to-validated-IP pinning. Unverified: ipaddress flags for IPv4-mapped IPv6 (::ffff:127.0.0.1) may not be caught.

verdict.guard_found: none closing. validators.py:12 is a scheme and hostname check, and validators.py:14-17 is an IP-range check on a single getaddrinfo result. Neither is hostname set membership or an anchored match, so neither closes the finding under the rubric. views.py:14 uses allow_redirects=False, which blocks redirect-based bypass but not DNS rebinding.
verdict.reason: The url comes from the unauthenticated query string at views.py:11, is_safe_url at views.py:12 resolves DNS once (validators.py:14) and only checks IP ranges, and requests.get at views.py:14 resolves the hostname again with no IP pinning, so a rebinding DNS answer can pass the check and reach an internal address. The IPv4-mapped IPv6 sub-claim is not verified here and is not needed for the verdict.
